Action approval

When does the publisher say actions require confirmation?

The 1.16.0 README describes always-ask as the default, always-approve or yolo as approving every action, and llm-approve as delegating approval decisions to an LLM-based security analyzer.

Authority · Change

Execution location

Does the CLI run locally or delegate to a hosted service?

The publisher describes terminal, ACP, headless and browser-served modes around the CLI, plus a cloud command that creates a hosted conversation. Rolling docs distinguish local compute and files from cloud compute and persistence.

Delegation

The publisher's current CLI cloud guide states that the openhands cloud command can authenticate to OpenHands Cloud or a custom server and create a hosted conversation from task text or a local file; the guide distinguishes cloud-hosted compute and cloud persistence from local CLI compute and local files.

Tool expansion

Can configuration add tools and destinations?

The tagged README describes HTTP, SSE and stdio MCP servers that can be added, enabled or disabled. Their tools, commands, credentials and destinations are configuration-specific.

Interoperability

The publisher's README at tag 1.16.0 states that OpenHands CLI can add, enable and disable MCP servers using HTTP, SSE or stdio transports, extending the tools available to the agent.

Configuration and history

What does the publisher say is stored locally?

Publisher sources name files under ~/.openhands for agent, CLI and MCP configuration and a conversations directory for local history. Environment overrides require an explicit flag and are described as not persisted.

Credentials

The publisher's README at tag 1.16.0 states that OpenHands CLI stores agent, CLI and MCP configuration under ~/.openhands, and ignores LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL and LLM_BASE_URL by default unless --override-with-envs is supplied, in which case those overrides are not persisted.

Record limitations

  • All substantive behavior statements are publisher-attributed; the catalog did not install or run OpenHands CLI.
  • Exact-version claims use the 1.16.0 release or tagged source; rolling documentation is not treated as exact-version evidence.
  • The dossier does not establish a wheel, source distribution, standalone binary, container or installed runtime digest.
  • The CLI surface can enter local, browser-served, ACP, container-backed and cloud modes; claims remain scoped rather than collapsed across them.
  • No independent report with defensible exact-version, artifact and configuration overlap was included.

Unresolved unknowns

What the admitted sources do not establish

Unknown does not mean absent. It means the accepted publisher sources do not establish the fact for an effective session.

  1. The package or binary artifact, platform build, digest and installation path used by any real user.
  2. The effective confirmation mode and whether every consequential action is covered by it.
  3. The LLM-based approval analyzer model, inputs, thresholds, availability and error behavior.
  4. The enabled built-in tools, hooks, skills, subagents and MCP servers in a particular session.
  5. The selected model provider, base URL, credentials, request payload and network destinations.
  6. The local workspace boundary, outside-workspace access, process environment and operating-system containment.
  7. The contents, permissions, encryption, retention, backup and deletion behavior of local conversation and configuration files.
  8. The cloud service's task upload scope, retention, deletion, training and downstream-provider behavior.
  9. Independent findings under overlapping 1.16.0 artifact and configuration applicability; none were included.
